paragraphs.text: Welcome, welcome, Sabbath morning, dear elders and sisters.
I hope you're all choosing to use your agency to act and not be acted upon today.

One of the most important things we need to learn in our mortal probation is the ability to rise above the cause-and-effect mindset that most people live in and suffer from. In the cause-and-effect mindset, people wait for some outside or external event to make them happy or sad, calm or worried, healthy or sick, rich or poor.
However, because God has given us agency, we have the power to cause an effect rather than just always being affected by some cause from outside ourselves.

In 2 Nephi 2:16, we are told: "Wherefore, the Lord God gave unto man that he should act for himself. Wherefore, man could not act for himself save it should be that he was enticed by the one or the other."

And we learn in verse 11 that opposition is essential for us so that we can actually exercise our agency. "For it must needs be, that there is an opposition in all things. If not so, my firstborn in the wilderness, righteousness could not be brought to pass, neither wickedness, neither holiness nor misery, neither good nor bad. Wherefore, all things must needs be a compound in one. Wherefore, if it should be one body, it must needs remain as dead, having no life neither death, nor corruption nor incorruption, happiness nor misery, neither sense nor insensibility."
As we look at this, we realize that the whole purpose of life is to learn how to deal with opposition in a way that brings blessings and good things to us.

Interestingly, later in 2 Nephi, Jacob teaches us about this by encouraging us to joyfully act for ourselves with this testimony: "Therefore, cheer up your hearts, and remember that ye are free to act for yourselves—to choose the way of everlasting death or the way of eternal life. Wherefore, my beloved brethren, reconcile yourselves to the will of God, and not to the will of the devil and the flesh; and remember, after ye are reconciled unto God, that it is only in and through the grace of God that ye are saved. Wherefore, may God raise you from death by the power of the resurrection, and also from everlasting death by the power of the atonement, that ye may be received into the eternal kingdom of God, that ye may praise him through grace divine. Amen."
In my life, I have learned that the best and easiest way to act for ourselves is found in the principle of gratitude.

When a person stays in a general state of gratitude, they literally stay in a state of receiving blessings. Good things just seem to keep happening to people who are always grateful. Even in their hardships, they find blessings. And as they stay in that state of consistent gratitude, they find they just keep getting more and more good things coming to them.
This must be why the scriptures are full of verses that command us to be grateful, because it is for our own good.
Consider these verses. Doctrine and Covenants 59:7: "Thou shalt thank the Lord thy God in all things."

Alma 34:38: "...that ye contend no more against the Holy Ghost, but that ye receive it, and take upon you the name of Christ; that ye humble yourselves even to the dust, and worship God, in whatsoever place ye may be in, in spirit and in truth; and that ye live in thanksgiving daily, for the many mercies and blessings which he doth bestow upon you."

This is one of my favorites. Doctrine and Covenants 78:19: "And he who receiveth all things with thankfulness shall be made glorious; and the things of this earth shall be added unto him, even an hundred fold, yea, more."
Now here's the principle to live by from Psalms 118:24. "This is the day which the Lord hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it."
So today really is the day the Lord hath made for each of us. Let us rejoice and be glad in it.

There's trouble and challenges, worries and all these different oppositions that are a part of our existence right now, but they're there by design to allow us to strengthen our ability to control our thoughts, exercise our agency, and prepare ourselves to receive more blessings for ourselves and for our families and loved ones.
God bless you, my dear fellow missionaries.
We are doing a great work, and we are being tested in the process.
We pray and exercise faith and hope and gratitude, and we will be blessed beyond measure today and forever, especially during this adventure we're going through right now.
We love you.
We're excited to serve with you.
Enjoy this day.
The Lord has made it for you.
